Carrier Logistics is partnering with LSP44 to automate shipment tracking for less-than-truckload carriers, including requests that arrive without a tracking number or with an incorrect one. The companies are developing an AI -powered connection designed to reduce the emails and phone calls carrier customer service teams must handle.
What’s Related
The collaboration lets shippers and third-party logistics providers find shipments by matching information they already have with records in a carrier’s transportation management system . That system is the software carriers use to manage freight and shipment records.
The companies are addressing what Carrier Logistics President Ben Wiesen calls “AI bot fatigue.” When automated tracking requests fail, bots turn to carrier customer service teams for answers, adding more messages and calls for employees to sort through.
“3PLs and shippers use APIs for shipment tracking, and these APIs are successful a majority of the time but are open to failing due to missing or incorrect tracking numbers,” Wiesen said. “This is where the bots step in, resulting in intrusive emails and phone calls that overwhelm the customer service teams at motor carriers.”
Finding shipments without a tracking number
The new connection uses an application programming interface, or API, which lets software systems exchange information directly. Instead of requiring a correct tracking number for every request, the AI matches known shipment details with shipments recorded in the carrier’s system.
According to the companies, that matching process can automatically resolve uncertainty about which shipment a customer is asking about. Shippers and 3PLs can then retrieve tracking information through the API, reducing the need to contact a carrier’s staff.
“With CLI’s new, AI-powered API, LTL carriers can provide the visibility their customers need without the added administrative burden and cost,” Wiesen said.
Reducing work for carrier service teams
Carrier Logistics provides freight management software for LTL carriers and other transportation businesses . Chicago-based LSP44 provides AI agents and software connections for 3PLs, freight forwarders, and brokers.
The companies say their joint engineering work is intended to make automated tracking more reliable and improve the accuracy of information passed along to customers. For carrier service teams, the goal is to reduce requests that require employees to find a shipment manually.
“The industry has treated manual tracking requests as the cost of doing business for decades,” said Nick Ruggiero, head of product at LSP44. “Every carrier running LTL has a customer service team absorbing that cost today.”
